acceptance_rule: At normal speed, both the motion and its observed direction must be recognizable in the unlabeled edited render before its answer is revealed. Every automatic and explicit direction variant must compare the exact source and edit, review and pass all required phases, explicitly verify the shared biomechanics and continuity checklist, and include a written evidence note. Numeric metrics cannot override a failed recognition, phase, biomechanics, or continuity review, and any failure blocks the production audit receipt.

clap_single.recognizable_as: one chest-level clap directed with the surrounding dance or to the requested side
required_phases: hands begin apart
both hands rise into a visible open guard before approaching each other
one visibly closed palm-to-palm contact is held long enough to read at chest level with relaxed diagonal fingers
the left and right contact points are unmistakably displaced from the forward clap; auto preserves source facing, while an explicit counter-flow side may use only a bounded upper-torso turn
the source root, torso, legs, and dance rhythm continue through the arm gesture
hands separate into the host dance

clap_repeat.recognizable_as: three chest-level claps directed with the surrounding dance or to the requested side
required_phases: hands rise to a chest-level guard
three visibly closed contacts each persist across multiple rendered frames with relaxed diagonal fingers and clear recoil
the requested left or right contact stays unmistakably displaced from the forward clap; only an explicit counter-flow side may add a bounded upper-torso turn
the source root, torso, legs, and dance rhythm continue throughout
hands stay near the guard between contacts
arms return without flapping to the hips
both arms rise above the head
palms visibly meet above the head for a readable contact hold without intersecting it
the overhead contact shifts unmistakably toward the requested or inferred direction; only an explicit counter-flow side may add a bounded upper-torso turn
the source root, torso, legs, and dance rhythm continue through the arm gesture
fingers continue the forearms through approach, contact, and recoil without wrist hyperextension or a hand-plane flip
hands separate through a smooth recoil without an elbow or wrist snap
arms lower into the host dance at a readable normal-speed duration
both legs narrow into a stable stance
hips and knees visibly load downward
both feet push off and leave the floor
the body reaches one clear apex
the load, flight, and landing remain individually readable at normal speed
both feet land with bent-knee absorption

jump_arms_up.recognizable_as: a two-foot jump with both arms raised
required_phases: hips and knees visibly load downward
both feet push off and leave the floor
both arms rise into a wide overhead V during flight and the hands never converge like a clap
the body reaches one clear apex
the load, flight, and landing remain individually readable at normal speed
both feet land with bent-knee absorption
the feet remain planted
knees and hips compress and extend repeatedly
the pelvis visibly changes height on each pulse
the torso retains the host groove
one hand rises above shoulder level
the raised hand changes direction repeatedly
the forearm and wrist remain connected
the hand lowers into the host dance

point_side.recognizable_as: a clear point to the side
required_phases: one arm prepares from the host pose
the arm extends dominantly sideways
the torso and head support the indicated direction
the arm retracts smoothly
the chest drives forward sharply
the pelvis remains comparatively stable
the source lower-body cadence, including any raised knee, remains intact without a squat or jump cue
the head does not turn the action into a nod
the chest recoils to the host pose
the punching arm prepares
the elbow extends dominantly forward
maximum forward reach lands on the declared musical event rather than before or after it
the torso counter-rotates into the hit
the arm retracts without becoming a side reach or locking the elbow

side_step.recognizable_as: a compact side step with a believable lateral weight transfer
required_phases: the lead foot lifts and opens a moderate distance laterally
the pelvis follows after the foot commits instead of dragging the whole body sideways
the torso counterbalances subtly while the source arms, head rhythm, and upper-body choreography continue
weight settles between the planted feet in a stable stance
the feet do not close into a trailing-foot touch
the lead foot steps laterally and accepts the weight
the root settles over the lead leg
the trailing foot lifts and taps close beside but slightly forward of the lead foot so both views retain separation
the root pauses and the touch holds briefly instead of continuing sideways
the lead foot swings and plants ahead
the root travels forward
the body follows the planted foot
the feet do not slide or moonwalk
the lead foot reaches and plants behind
the root travels backward
the body follows the planted foot
the action is visibly opposite to step_forward
the body prepares through the feet and hips
the whole body rotates about 90 degrees
the feet support the new facing
the turn resolves without a yaw whip
the body prepares through the feet and hips
the whole body rotates about 180 degrees
the head and torso spot the turn
the turn resolves facing the opposite direction
the wave begins in the hips or lower torso with a visible crest and release
an S-curve travels sequentially through the spine rather than stacking same-direction bends
the chest and upper torso crest after the hips have begun to release
the action does not read as one rigid bow or lean
the body anticipates before both hips and knees bend
the pelvis clearly lowers while the hips fold back and the knees remain supported over planted feet
the torso inclines as one connected line while the head keeps a forward gaze
the feet remain planted
the low pose is held briefly rather than freezing for the rest of the action
a controlled recovery begins before the motion hands back to the host dance

rise_reach.recognizable_as: a rise with an upward reach
required_phases: the action begins from a visibly low level
the legs extend while the torso rises
both arms reach upward with one hand visibly beginning and leading forward before the other
the feet remain planted so the action does not become a jump
